summary: Master Program and Budget Analysis with our comprehensive Microsoft Excel course. Gain practical skills to optimize budgets and improve financial performance.
lede: Program and budget analysis in Excel connects program plans with resource decisions by organizing financial and performance data. For program managers, budget analysts, and finance business partners, it supports building budget baselines, cleaning and classifying data, and examining actual-versus-budget results. Practical work includes allocating shared costs, forecasting and testing funding scenarios, and presenting KPIs and recommendations in dashboards and analysis packs.
audienceIntro: This program and budget analysis course suits professionals who prepare, review, manage, or communicate program resource decisions in Excel. It supports foundation to intermediate learners who can work with basic spreadsheets and want a more disciplined approach to financial and performance analysis.
prerequisites: You should have basic Microsoft Excel experience, including entering data, using simple formulas, sorting, filtering, and creating basic charts. No programming or VBA knowledge is required. Familiarity with program planning, departmental budgets, expenditure reporting, or performance indicators will help, but you do not need formal accounting certification. Advanced functions such as Power Query, Solver, PivotTables, and sensitivity analysis are introduced progressively and practised with provided datasets.
